name: Field Doctor-Style Smokey Chipotle Meatballs (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
1 1/2 x 400 g tins Plum Tomato
615 g Extra Lean Beef
480 g Potato
1 1/2 medium Sweet Potatoes
1/4 Green Peppers
1/2 medium Carrots
2 1/2 tbsp Tomato Puree [tomato]
5 tbsp Quinoa Flour
35 g Red Quinoa
1 1/2 tbsp Tapioca Starch
3 1/2 tbsp Mixed Herbs
1 1/4 tbsp Cumin Ground
8.6 g Quinoa Flake
1 1/4 tbsp Parmigiano (MILK) [MILK Salt, Microbial Enzymes]
1 1/4 tbsp Flax Seeds
1 3/4 tsp Beef Stock [Beef Extract, Water, Salt]
4.3 g Chives
3/4 tsp Red Wine Vinegar
1 1/2 tsp Smoked Paprika
1/2 tsp Tamari [water, SOYA beans, sea salt]
1/2 tsp Sea Salt
1 1/4 tsp Sweet Noble Paprika
1 1/4 tsp Chipotle chilli
1/3 tsp Celery Salt (CELERY)
2/3 tsp Black Pepper
1/2 tsp Oregano
directions:
1. Meatballs: Mix beef with quinoa flour, quinoa flakes, flax seeds, hard cheese, cumin, paprika, oregano, celery salt, black pepper, chives and a little tamari. Form into meatballs.

2. Brown meatballs in extra virgin olive oil; set aside.

3. Sauce: Soften green pepper and carrot with chives. Add chopped tomato, tomato puree, chipotle, smoked paprika, sweet paprika, red wine vinegar, beef stock and oregano. Simmer until rich; thicken with tapioca slurry if needed.

4. Potatoes: Meanwhile boil potato and sweet potato until tender; drain and keep warm (or lightly crush with oil and salt).

5. Finish: Simmer meatballs in the chipotle tomato sauce until cooked through. Serve with the potatoes; garnish with chives.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.
description:
Ingredients: Water, Chopped Tomato, Extra Lean Beef, Potato, Sweet Potato, Green Pepper, Carrot, Extra Virgin Olive Oil...

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Smokey Chipotle Meatballs (Low FODMAP) (~367 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/smokey-chipotle-meatballs
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~367 g x 8 = 2936 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~641 g (inferred ~21.84% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Oil for home cooking: where Extra Virgin Olive Oil was only a cooking fat on the label, it is omitted from ingredients — fry, soften, sear or roast in extra virgin olive oil as needed. It is kept as an ingredient on richer/oil-forward dishes (e.g. pesto-style sauces or high oil content).
Ready-meal residual Extra Virgin Olive Oil was ~42 g (inferred ~1.42% from list order) and is treated as cooking fat (fry in extra virgin olive oil) rather than a measured ingredient.
